attempted_claim: Let d>=9 and let W be the energy-critical biharmonic ground state Delta^2 W=|W|^{8/(d-4)}W. For i u_t + Delta^2 u = |u|^{8/(d-4)} u with conserved E(u)=1/2||Delta u||_2^2-(d-4)/(2d)||u||_{2d/(d-4)}^{2d/(d-4)}, prove for non-radial dot-H^2 data with E(u0)<E(W): (i) ||Delta u0||_2<||Delta W||_2 implies the maximal solution is global with finite scattering size iint|u|^{2(d+4)/(d-4)}<=C<infinity and scatters in dot-H^2 both directions; (ii) ||Delta u0||_2>||Delta W||_2 plus finite variance implies finite-time blow-up in at least one direction. In particular prove sup_{t in I}||Delta u(t)||_2<||Delta W||_2 => S_I(u)<=C without radial assumption in d>=9.
decisive_failure: No scattering or blow-up dichotomy is proved. Verified fragments are limited to the standard sharp-Sobolev trapping split and the formal finite-variance virial sign, which are textbook facts with no originality. The uniform non-radial scattering bound and rigorous virial justification remain open; no artifacts beyond the worklog and exit records are claimed.
